Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Hon'ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
(Per: Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
Mr. Ashish Joshi, Advocate for the appellants.
2. Mr. Vinod Chandra Joshi, Advocate, holding
brief of Ms. Neetu Singh, Advocate for the
respondent no. 1.
3. Mr. K.N. Joshi, Deputy Advocate General for
the State/respondent no. 2.
4. There is 4 days delay in filing the special
appeal. For the reasons indicated in the delay
condonation application, we are inclined to condone
the delay of 4 days in filing the appeal. Accordingly,
delay condonation application is allowed.
5. Uttarakhand Transport Corporation has filed
this Appeal, challenging the judgment dated
20.02.2018, rendered by learned Single Judge in Writ
Petition (S/S) No. 132 of 2015. By the said judgment,
order of rejection passed by authorities of
Uttarakhand Transport Corporation was quashed and
they were directed to consider case of the writ
petitioner (respondent no. 1 herein) for compassionate
appointment, in accordance with law, without being
influenced by the delay.
6. It is not in dispute that father of respondent no.
1 (writ petitioner), who was serving as Driver on
regular basis in Uttarakhand Transport Corporation,
died in harness on 26.06.2008. Respondent no. 1

2025:UHC:6611-DB
made application for compassionate appointment on
08.10.2013 with delay of 103 days.
7. As per applicable Rules, request for
compassionate appointment has to be made within
five years from the date of death, however, in
appropriate cases, an application for compassionate
appointment can be accepted even after five years.
8. Respondent No. 1 in his writ petition explained
the delay by submitting that there was a ban imposed
by the State Government on compassionate
appointments in Uttarakhand Transport Corporation,
which was enforced in the year 2001 and remained
effective till 13.09.2013; respondent applied for
compassionate appointment thereafter, on 08.10.2013.
9. Learned Single Judge, by applying the
principle of Lex non cogit ad impossibilia allowed the
writ petition by holding that respondent cannot be
forced to do the impossible by submitting the
application, when there was complete ban on
compassionate appointments.
10. We concur with the reasoning given by learned
Single Judge. Respondent No. 1 cannot be blamed for
delay of 103 days, when there was a ban on
compassionate appointments, imposed by the State
Government.
11. In such view of the matter, the Special Appeal
fails and is dismissed.
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
